recommendation: Keep the source fix. Do not change integer64 from xsd:long to bare xsd:integer unless FHIR-I explicitly decides to relax RDF/ShEx range validation; handle any future generated-artifact divergence in the Kindling/publisher generator path.
issue_request: FHIR-25622 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR core in R5 and requested RDF generator and ShEx tooling support for the integer64 datatype, described as mapping into the XML Schema integer family and being treated like integer.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly tagged FHIR-25622 was found. Current R5 and current generated ShEx and RDF ontology artifacts already include integer64 and use xsd:long with signed 64-bit constraints, apparently flowing from the existing integer64 primitive source. The remaining source gap was that source/rdf.html's fhir:v datatype list did not mention derived integer datatypes such as xsd:long.
additional_context: The related FHIR-25208 audit on the combined branch confirmed current core integer64 semantics as signed 64-bit with xs:long and JSON string representation. Because xsd:long is derived from xsd:integer, preserving xsd:long keeps the range constraint while satisfying the integer-family RDF/ShEx intent.
reconciliation: Changed source/rdf.html to include integer-derived XSD datatypes such as int, long, and positiveInteger in the primitive literal datatype list, aligning narrative RDF guidance with generated ShEx and ontology output without weakening integer64 to unbounded xsd:integer.
source_changes: source/rdf.html: added integer-derived XSD datatypes such as int, long, and positiveInteger to the fhir:v primitive literal datatype list.

related_jiras.note: Established and audited the current integer64 datatype semantics as signed 64-bit with xs:long and JSON string representation.
Mapped FHIR.integer64 to a 64-bit integer type in FHIRPath, supporting the range-preserving interpretation.
Clarified JSON serialization for newer integer types and retained integer64 as a JSON string.
